description: The graph illustrates the performance of various models in terms of Area Under the Curve (AUC) percentage as a function of the parameter N, which likely represents the number of samples or a related metric. The y-axis is labeled "AUC (%)" and ranges from 75 to 100, with a linear scale, while the x-axis is labeled "N" and ranges from 0 to 20, also on a linear scale. Five distinct lines, each represented by a different color and marker, show the trend of AUC for different models or configurations. The blue line, marked with circles, starts at approximately 94% AUC at N=0, increases to 99% at N=5, and then slightly decreases to around 97% at N=20. The orange line, marked with diamonds, begins at about 84% AUC at N=0, rises to 99% at N=10, and then declines to approximately 95% at N=20. The green line, marked with stars, starts at around 86% AUC at N=0, increases to about 94% at N=10, and then slightly decreases to 93% at N=20. The red line, marked with squares, starts at approximately 87% AUC at N=0, increases to 99% at N=10, and then decreases to about 91% at N=20. The purple line, marked with triangles, starts at around 79% AUC at N=0, increases to 98% at N=10, and then sharply declines to about 82% at N=20. The gray square in the legend does not correspond to any line in the plot, suggesting it may represent a baseline or reference value not plotted.
